author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How PCSX2 handles GS texture shuffles and blending
summary: PCSX2 recognizes blending, texture-shuffle and framebuffer patterns that otherwise produce artifacts when translated to modern graphics APIs.
heroAlt: How PCSX2 handles GS texture shuffles and blending
searchKeywords: How PCSX2 handles GS texture shuffles and blending

blocks.text: Texture shuffles expose GS memory tricks

PlayStation 2 games can reinterpret framebuffer channels and memory layouts to build effects with limited GS resources. PCSX2 improved detection for pixel reversals, sprites whose width is not a 16-pixel multiple, palette shuffles and offset-shuffle cases.

Many shadows, lights and transparencies read values that were already rendered. Modern APIs differ in how safely and efficiently they expose that feedback. PCSX2 chooses barriers, render passes or readbacks according to backend capability while preserving the blend equation the game expects.

The renderer uses a CRC for the palette-shuffle effect used by Sand Grain games and refined `TexIsFB` offset-shuffle detection. These identifiers select narrow handling for demonstrated workloads instead of raising an expensive accuracy mode globally.

Vulkan, Direct3D and OpenGL do not offer identical feedback and ordering features. Hardware results are compared with the software renderer and native-resolution captures, then each backend implements the safest equivalent available on the host GPU.

The goal is to keep effects correct on the hardware renderer so users can retain upscaling and modern presentation. Moving more shuffle and blend cases out of manual workarounds also makes results less dependent on a user's old per-game configuration. Narrow detection is essential because a broad workaround can repair one effect while corrupting ordinary draws elsewhere. Test captures must preserve the same scene, internal resolution and backend, with software output serving as a reference rather than a permanent fallback. Once the triggering GS pattern is understood, PCSX2 can keep the correction local and retain hardware rendering performance for the rest of the frame.
